_readme: Assumption basis register (v4.2). One entry per assumption in code/python/npv_assumptions.json (a key ending in * covers the whole block; its value is the block without documentation strings). status: P = public source, S = statute / regulation, D = derived for internal consistency, J = judgment (needs a sensitivity range), E = company experience (none shipped), M = model setting. Policy: the synthetic book is not relevant experience for a Humana block (ASOP 25 §3.3), so no credibility is given to its experience. synthetic_link discloses the exceptions: 'derived' = a distribution input read off the synthetic book (sales mix, category shares, Medicaid cell mix); 'equals_generator' = the value equals the synthetic generator's own and is retained because the cited public figure supports it, so the source is a reasonableness check rather than the derivation. tests/test_v4_model.py fails if any assumption is missing here, if a value differs from the documented one, if a P/S entry has no source, or if a J entry has no sensitivity range. docs/ASSUMPTION_BASIS.md is generated from this file.

entries.basis: Category shares from the (synthetic) service mix; neutral category trend and pent-up; no waiting periods, matching the product the experience reflects. Market norm is 6/12-month waiting periods on basic/major (EMI); the engine defers a waited category's pent-up demand to the first 12 months after the wait ends (v4.1), so a waiting-period design can be tested as a product option. The shares have NO effect on the base results (categories are neutral); they scale only the waiting-period options (dv_product_options.csv, MAJOR share 24.9%).
